texts.orig: The plan now is to first excise the non-isolated leaves of A from S, producing a surface with boundary So < S where AnS0 consists only of isolated geodesic arcs, each of which is compact. We then split So into a number of "regions" Ri by cutting the "critical arcs." By applying the Poincaré-Hopf theorem to the vector field X restricted to a region Ri, we show that at least one of these regions has positive Euler characteristic and therefore must be a topological disk. Its pre-image (Ri) must contain half of a vertical leaf of gcu_ and this causes a contradiction; completing the overall proof. along
